title: Creamy Spinach Soft Scramble

steps.text: Whisk the eggs and milk together in a bowl until frothy and pale.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat and wilt the spinach until just collapsed and glossy.
Pour in the eggs and scrape slowly with a spatula as soft curds pile up.
Pull the pan off the heat and let the cheese melt through in ribbons.
Serve when a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the thickest spoonful, with the yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Garlic Butter Mushrooms on Golden Toast

steps.text: Toast the bread until deep golden and crisp, then keep it warm.
Melt the butter in a skillet and let the minced garlic sizzle until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the mushrooms in one layer and let them brown at the edges, about 5 minutes, moving them only now and then.
Pile the buttery mushrooms onto the toast.
Spoon every last bit of garlic butter from the pan over the top.

title: Warm Peanut Butter Banana Oatmeal Bowl

steps.text: Warm the milk in a small pot until it steams at the edges.
Add the oats and give them 2 minutes to swell into something thick and creamy.
Swirl the peanut butter through so it melts into ribbons.
Let the bowl sit a minute to thicken to your liking.
Fan the sliced banana over the top and eat warm.

title: Make-Ahead Apple Yogurt Oat Jar

steps.text: Give the oats and yogurt a good stir in a jar until every oat is coated.
Dice half the apple small and stir it through with the honey.
Loosen with a splash of water, cover, and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, top the jar with the remaining diced apple.

title: Layered Honey Apple Yogurt Cup

steps.text: Dice the apple into small cubes, skin on or off.
Layer yogurt, apple, and oats in a glass, spooning each layer to the edge so it shows.
Repeat the layers once more, ending with a thin thread of honey.
Let the cup sit for 5 minutes so the oats soften slightly.

title: Smashed Avocado Toast with Soft Poached Eggs

steps.text: Toast the bread until deep golden.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, leaving it chunky.
Slide the eggs into gently simmering, swirled water and cook 3 minutes.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon and check that a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center, with the yolk and white firm; give them another minute in the water if it reads low.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Spread the avocado thickly on the toast and crown with the eggs.
Finish with a final squeeze of lemon.

title: Crispy Potato Breakfast Skillet with Eggs and Cheese

steps.text: Dice the potato small and fry in the olive oil over medium heat until the edges turn crisp and brown, 10 to 12 minutes.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft, sweet, and lightly golden.
Make two wells in the hash and crack an egg into each.
Cover the pan and cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the thickest white, with the yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Scatter the cheese over the top and let it melt off the heat.
Bring the whole skillet to the table.

title: Sunrise Egg and Black Bean Tortilla Wraps

steps.text: Warm the black beans in a small pot, mashing a few against the side so they turn creamy.
Melt half the butter in a pan and scramble the eggs slowly over low heat, checking that a food thermometer reads 160 °F; the yolk and white should both be firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until pliable and freckled.
Pile the eggs, beans, and cheese down the middle of each tortilla.
Roll tightly, then set them seam-side down in the pan for a minute to seal.

title: Soy-Seasoned Morning Oats with Jammy Eggs

steps.text: Simmer the oats with double their volume of water, stirring now and then, until creamy and loose.
Boil the eggs for 6 minutes, then check one with an instant-read thermometer: it should register 160 °F, with the yolk and white firm; add a minute if it reads low.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Cool the eggs under cold water, peel, and halve.
Season the oats with the soy sauce and spoon them into bowls.
Nestle the egg halves on top and scatter over the green onion.

title: Cumin-Scented Tofu Breakfast Scramble

steps.text: Crumble the tofu with your hands into bite-size bits and pat dry.
Soften the diced bell pepper and onion in the olive oil until slumped and sweet, about 5 minutes.
Add the tofu with the cumin, pressing it against the pan with a spatula so it catches and steams.
Cook until the tofu is flecked golden at the edges and smells nutty, 4 to 5 minutes.
Taste and serve straight from the pan.

title: Open-Faced Tomato Cheese Toast with Olive Oil

steps.text: Toast the bread until deep golden and crisp at the rim.
Slice the tomatoes and let them sit a few minutes so their juices bead.
Spread a generous layer of cheese over the warm toast.
Shingle the tomato slices on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and eat while the toast still crackles.

title: Peanut Butter Banana Sushi Rolls

steps.text: Give the tortilla a few seconds of heat so it rolls without cracking.
Spread the peanut butter edge to edge.
Lay the banana in a firm line down the middle.
Roll it up tight and slice into thick coins, like sushi.

title: Skillet Tomato Eggs with Toast Dippers

steps.text: Soften the diced onion in the butter until sweet and glossy.
Chop the tomatoes and simmer them into a thick, jammy sauce, about 10 minutes.
Make two wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until a quick thermometer check registers 160 °F in the thickest white — yolk and white both firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Toast the bread, cut it into strips, and serve alongside for dipping.

title: Seared Salmon Toast with Lemon Cucumbers

steps.text: Toast the bread until deep golden.
Shave the cucumber into thin ribbons and toss with a little lemon.
Sear the salmon in a hot nonstick pan, about four minutes on the first side.
Flip and cook two minutes more, then check with a food thermometer until it reads 145 °F at the thickest point.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-15

steps.text: Spread the cheese over the warm toast, flake the salmon on top, and pile the cucumber ribbons alongside.
Finish with a last squeeze of lemon.

title: Banana Oat Pancakes with Browned Butter

steps.text: Mash the bananas until smooth and glossy.
Whisk in the eggs, milk, and oats to a thick, nubbly batter.
Rest the batter 5 minutes so the oats drink and thicken it.
Cook ladlefuls in butter over medium heat until bubbles pop across the surface and the edges look dry, then flip and brown the other side.
Check the first pancake against a food thermometer: it should register 160 °F in the center; lower the heat if the outsides color first.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Melt a knob of butter until it foams and smells toasty, then pour it over the stack.

title: Muffin Tin Zucchini Egg Bites

steps.text: Grate the zucchini and squeeze out the water with your hands until it stops dripping.
Get the oven heating while you work.
Whisk the eggs, then season them.
Divide the zucchini, onion, and cheese between six muffin cups and pour the eggs over.
Bake about 15 minutes, until puffed; they are ready when a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center of a cup and the yolk and white are firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: French-Style Rolled Omelette with Buttery Mushrooms and Spinach

steps.text: Cook the mushrooms in half the butter until browned and dry, then add the spinach and let it just wilt; tip onto a plate.
Whisk the eggs until smooth and pour into a wide, buttered pan over low heat.
Tilt and pull the setting curds toward the middle so it builds into one thin, even sheet.
Let it finish gently until a thermometer probe reads 160 °F and the whites have firmed around the yolk; the surface should stay barely glossy.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Lay the vegetables along one edge and roll the omelette over them, then slide it onto a plate seam-side down.

title: Crispy-Edged Sweet Potato Hash with Eggs

steps.text: Dice the sweet potato small and fry in the olive oil, covered, until tender, about 10 minutes.
Uncover, raise the heat, and let the cubes brown and crisp at the edges.
Add the diced bell pepper and onion and cook until softened and charred in spots.
In a second pan, fry the eggs until a thermometer held in the whites reaches 160 °F, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Pile the hash into bowls and top with the eggs.

title: Cool Cucumber Ribbon Toast with Green Onion

steps.text: Toast the bread thickly so it holds up.
Spread a generous layer of cheese right to the corners.
Shave the cucumber into long ribbons and pile them on in soft folds.
Scatter the green onion over and press gently so everything holds.

title: Creamy Apple Rice Pudding for Breakfast

steps.text: Simmer the cooked rice in the milk, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 12 minutes.
Grate in the apple, stopping shy of the core.
Sweeten with the honey and finish with the butter, stirred through until glossy.
Warm 2 minutes more so the apple softens into the pudding.
Serve warm with extra grated apple scattered on top.

title: Wok-Charred Chicken Fried Rice with Fresh Ginger

steps.text: Heat a wok over high heat until it just smokes, add the chicken in one layer, and cook until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest piece. Move it to a plate.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Scramble the eggs in the same wok until a food thermometer reads 160 °F and the yolk and white are firm, then push them to one side.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Add the cold cooked rice and press and toss until every grain is separate and sizzling.
Return the chicken with the grated ginger and toss until the pan steams and the ginger perfumes everything.
Scatter the green onion over and serve hot.

title: Sesame-Glazed Crispy Tofu with Broccoli

steps.text: Press the tofu dry and cut it into bite-size cubes.
Fry in a wide pan over medium-high heat until deep golden and crackly on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the broccoli with a splash of water, cover, and steam 2 minutes until vivid green and tender-crisp.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the soy sauce and sesame oil, tossing until everything gleams.
Serve hot from the pan.

title: Weeknight Beef and Bell Pepper Noodle Toss

steps.text: Cook the pasta until just tender, reserve a cup of the water, and drain.
Brown the ground beef in a screaming-hot pan, crumbling as it browns, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Add the sliced bell pepper and garlic and cook until the pepper slumps and the garlic smells sweet.
Add the pasta with the soy sauce and a splash of its cooking water; toss well.
Keep everything moving about a minute, until glossy and clinging.

title: Silken Tomato Coconut Curry with Chickpeas

steps.text: Soften the diced onion and garlic in a heavy pot over medium heat until sweet and glassy, adding a splash of water if they stick.
Add the chopped tomato and cook it down to a dark, rough paste, 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and coconut milk, scraping the base clean.
Simmer 15 minutes, until thickened and settled.
Taste and ladle into deep bowls.

title: Deeply Savory Mushroom Noodle Broth with Green Onion

steps.text: Bring 700 ml water to a simmer with the soy sauce, garlic, and mushrooms, and let it steep 8 minutes, until the broth smells earthy.
Cook the pasta directly in the broth until just tender.
Taste and balance with a further splash of soy sauce.
Ladle into deep bowls.
Scatter the green onion over the top.

title: Sticky Honey-Ginger Chicken Rice Bowls

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Pan-fry the chicken over medium-high heat until deeply browned outside and a food thermometer inserted in the thickest piece reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Stir the soy sauce, honey, and grated ginger together in a cup.
Pour the glaze over the chicken and let it bubble and thicken, spooning it over, until sticky and lacquered.
Rest the chicken a few minutes, slice, and pile onto the rice.
Spoon the extra glaze over and serve.

title: Crackly-Fried Tofu Rice Bowl with Cool Cucumber

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Cube the tofu and press it dry until it squeaks.
Fry in a wide pan until crackly and deep golden on all sides.
Toss the hot tofu with the soy sauce and sesame oil.
Slice the cucumber thin and build bowls of rice, tofu, and cucumber.

title: Velvety Egg Ribbon Soup with Green Onion

steps.text: Heat the milk with the same volume of water until it steams, but don't let it boil.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl until smooth.
Swirl the pot in one direction and drizzle the eggs through in a thin stream.
Wait 20 seconds without stirring, then break the ribbons apart gently.
Give the pot 30 seconds more if a food thermometer doesn't reach 160 °F; yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Ladle into bowls and finish with the green onion and a little butter.

title: Glossy Honey-Garlic Glazed Salmon

steps.text: Pat the salmon dry so it sears instead of steams.
Sear skin-side down 4 minutes, until the skin is crisp and releases easily.
Flip and add the garlic and ginger, letting them sizzle until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the honey and soy sauce and spoon the bubbling glaze over the fish.
Rest 2 minutes off the heat, then check that a food thermometer slipped into the thickest part reads 145 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Garlicky Peanut Noodles with Sesame Oil

steps.text: Cook the pasta until just tender, reserving a cup of the water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, and grated garlic with enough hot water to make a smooth, pourable sauce.
Toss the warm pasta through the sauce, loosening with the cooking water until it coats every strand.
Eat warm, or chill and serve cold later the same day.

title: Garlicky Ginger Greens over Steamed Rice

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Toast the garlic and ginger in a hot, dry pan for half a minute, until fragrant.
Add the broccoli with a splash of water, cover, and steam until vivid green and just tender, about 3 minutes.
Toss in the spinach until it just wilts and turns glossy.
Spoon the greens and their pan juices over the rice.

title: Hometown Ginger Chicken Congee

steps.text: Rinse the rice, then simmer it in 1.2 litres of water, stirring often so it doesn't catch.
After 15 minutes, add the chicken diced small with the ginger and garlic.
Simmer gently about 35 minutes total, until the grains break down and the pot turns creamy; the congee is ready when a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest spoonful of chicken.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Ladle into bowls and top with the green onion.
Chill leftovers up to four days; reheat portions until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Golden Fried Rice with Sweet Peas

steps.text: Scramble the eggs in hot olive oil until softly curdled — a food thermometer should register 160 °F with the yolk and white firm — then slide them onto a plate.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Fry the cold rice in the same pan, pressing it against the hot surface until it squeaks and smells nutty.
Add the peas and toss until bright and steaming.
Return the eggs and break them into pieces with the spatula.
Scatter the green onion over and serve.

title: Fiery Crumbled Tofu with Soy and Garlic

steps.text: Crumble the tofu into rough, bite-size bits.
Dry-fry it in a hot pan until golden at the edges and squeaky, about 6 minutes.
Add the diced onion, garlic, and red pepper flakes and cook until the onion slumps.
Season with the soy sauce and a splash of water and simmer until the sauce clings to every bit.
Spoon into bowls and eat hot.

title: Cool Lime Chicken Salad with Cucumber and Carrot

steps.text: Slip the chicken into gently simmering water and poach until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest piece. Cool slightly, then shred along the grain.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Cut the cucumber and carrot into fine matchsticks.
Dress the vegetables with the lime juice.
Toss the shredded chicken with the vegetables and torn cilantro.
Taste and add another squeeze of lime; it should be bright and sharp.

title: Lacquer-Glazed Tofu over Steamed Rice

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Pan-fry the tofu cubes in a nonstick pan until browned on all sides.
Stir the honey, soy sauce, and crushed garlic together with a spoonful of water.
Pour over the tofu and let it reduce to a dark, clinging lacquer.
Serve the tofu and its glaze over the rice.

title: Sizzling Tomato Rice with Crispy-Edged Egg

steps.text: Fry the chopped tomato in a hot pan until it slumps into a jammy sauce.
Season with the soy sauce and red pepper flakes.
Add the cold cooked rice and toss until every grain is coated and sizzling.
Push the rice aside and crack the egg into the middle, then cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F; the yolk and white should be firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Serve with the egg settled on top.

title: Takeout-Style Beef and Broccoli at Home

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it warm.
Get a hot pan ripping and brown the ground beef hard, breaking it up as it browns, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Throw in the garlic for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the broccoli with a splash of water, clamp on a lid, and steam 3 minutes, until vivid green and just tender.
Add the soy sauce and toss until everything is glossy and clinging; serve over the rice.

title: Chirashi-Style Avocado Cucumber Rice Bowl

steps.text: Season the warm cooked rice with the soy sauce.
Dice the avocado and cucumber into neat cubes.
Arrange them over the rice in loose drifts.
Taste and add a further dash of soy sauce if it needs it.
Scatter the green onion over and eat with a spoon, like a deconstructed roll.

title: Salmon Steamed in Foil with Lemon and Ginger

steps.text: Start the oven heating first.
Lay the salmon on a large sheet of foil with the zucchini sliced into coins.
Top with the lemon slices, grated ginger, and olive oil.
Seal the parcel tightly so no steam can escape.
Cook 15 minutes, then open carefully and check that a food thermometer in the thickest part reads 145 °F; spoon the juices over.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Sesame Soy Noodles with Wilted Spinach and Egg

steps.text: Set a generous pot of water boiling and cook the pasta until springy with a faint bite at the center, then drain it well.
Return the empty pot to medium-high heat, add the sesame oil, and wait until it shimmers and smells faintly nutty.
Tear in the spinach a handful at a time, tossing just until it slumps into glossy dark ribbons, a minute or so.
Slide the pasta in with the soy sauce and toss over the heat until every noodle shines and the pan smells toasty and savory.

Push the noodles to one side, pour the egg into the empty half, and scramble it gently until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the softest curd, then break the egg into ribbons and toss it through the pasta.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Pull the pot off the heat, add a last drizzle of sesame oil, and eat straight away while the noodles are hot.

title: Lemon-Dressed Chickpeas with Crunchy Cucumber

steps.text: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, then tip them into a wide bowl.
Cut the cucumber into fat half-moons and the tomato into rough chunks, keeping the pieces big enough to stay juicy.
Dress with lemon juice and olive oil, season boldly, and turn everything together with your hands or a big spoon.
Let the salad sit ten minutes so the lemon finds its way into the chickpeas and the tomato juices loosen into the dressing.
Taste once more before serving; it should taste bright and a little sharper than feels polite.

title: Jammy Tomato Skillet Eggs

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet and cook the sliced bell pepper with the garlic until the pepper slumps and turns sweet-smelling, five or six minutes.
Add the chopped tomato and let it bubble down until the sauce thickens and darkens, mounding slowly on a spoon, about ten minutes.
Season the sauce well and make two shallow wells in it with the back of a spoon.
Crack an egg into each well, cover the pan, and cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center of an egg, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Bring the skillet to the table and spoon the extra sauce over each egg before eating.

title: Pan-Seared Chicken with Lemony Zucchini Coins

steps.text: Pat the chicken breast dry and season it well on both sides.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and lay the chicken in without crowding; let it sear undisturbed until the underside is deeply golden, about five minutes.
Flip and keep cooking until a food thermometer reads 165 °F at the thickest point, then move the chicken to a plate to rest.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Add the zucchini coins and garlic to the empty pan and cook until tender at the edge and spotted with gold, catching the pan juices as you go.
Squeeze in the lemon and scrape up the browned bits, then spoon the zucchini onto plates and set the chicken on top.

title: Lemony Tuna and Chickpea Desk Lunch

steps.text: Drain the canned light tuna and the chickpeas well and tip both into a wide bowl.
Slice the celery as thin as you can, on a sharp angle, so it stays crisp without taking over.
Dress with lemon juice and olive oil and season generously.
Break the tuna into big, rough pieces with a fork and turn everything together gently, keeping some texture in the tuna.
Let it sit five minutes so the celery loses a little of its bite, then pack it up or eat it now.

title: Chunky Tomato Salad with Crumbled Cheese

steps.text: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and the cucumber into thick half-moons; slice the bell pepper into rough strips.
Slice the onion paper-thin and soak it in cold water for five minutes to tame its edge, then drain.
Toss the vegetables with olive oil and a good grind of seasoning.
Crumble the cheese over the top in big, uneven pieces.
Let it stand a few minutes so the tomato juices and oil pool together, then serve.

title: One-Tray Salmon with Blistered Broccoli

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C and toss the broccoli with olive oil and the garlic on a rimmed tray.
Nestle the salmon among the florets and drizzle it with a little more oil.
Roast twelve to fifteen minutes, until a food thermometer registers 145 °F at the thickest part of the salmon.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Finish with lemon juice over the whole tray and serve hot, catching the pan juices with the broccoli.

title: Zucchini Simmered Soft with Chickpeas and Tomato

steps.text: Soften the diced onion in olive oil over medium heat until it turns glassy and sweet, six or seven minutes.
Add the chopped zucchini and tomato and cook until they start to release their juices.
Add the chickpeas and half a glass of water, then leave everything to simmer gently.
Simmer about twenty minutes, until the zucchini goes silky and the sauce turns thick enough to coat a spoon.
Season well, then rest the pan off the heat a few minutes before serving; it is good warm or at room temperature.

title: Cold Garlic Yogurt with Grated Cucumber

steps.text: Grate the cucumber coarsely, then squeeze it hard in your hands or a clean towel until most of the water is out.
Stir the cucumber into the yogurt with the crushed garlic.
Add a thread of olive oil and season well.
Chill it ten minutes if you can spare the time; the garlic mellows as it sits.
Serve it cold as a cool, garlicky side for anything rich or spiced.

title: Lemony Rice with Wilted Spinach

steps.text: Soften the diced onion in olive oil in a lidded pan until it turns glassy and sweet.
Add the rice and turn it through the oil until the grains look chalky and smell lightly toasted.
Pour in hot water to cover by about a finger's width and season.
Cover and simmer gently until the rice is tender and the water is gone, about fifteen minutes.
Take off the heat and add the spinach, lemon juice, and a drizzle of olive oil; return the lid for two minutes so the spinach wilts, then fluff with a fork.

title: Roasted Tomato Halves with Chickpeas and Spinach

steps.text: Halve the tomatoes and scoop out the juicy centers, keeping the shells intact; heat the oven to 190°C.
Chop the scooped centers and toss them with the chickpeas, spinach, garlic, and olive oil; season well.
Spoon the filling back into the tomato shells, mounding it generously.
Roast twenty-five to thirty minutes, until the tomato edges caramelize and the filling is hot and steaming.
Serve warm, straight from the tray.

title: Tomato-Rubbed Toast the Spanish Way

steps.text: Toast or griddle the bread until the outside is crisp and the middle still has a little chew.
Cut the garlic clove in half and rub the cut side firmly over the hot surface of the toast.
Press a halved tomato cut-side down against the bread, squeezing until the flesh soaks in and the crust glistens.
Season and drizzle with your best olive oil.
Eat immediately, while the edges are still crackly.

title: Golden Garlic Tuna Pasta

steps.text: Cook the pasta in a big pot of water until springy with a faint bite, reserving a cup of the cooking water before draining.
Warm the olive oil with the garlic in the empty pot until the garlic smells fragrant, then add the canned light tuna and lemon juice and let it heat gently for a minute.
Add the pasta and a splash of the cooking water and toss hard until the sauce turns silky and clings to the noodles.
Add more cooking water a splash at a time if it tightens up; it should flow slowly, not sit in a lump.
Season heavily and serve at once.

title: Deep-Browned Zucchini over Garlic Yogurt

steps.text: Cut the zucchini into thick batons, toss with olive oil and the garlic, and spread them out on a tray; heat the oven to 220°C.
Roast twenty to twenty-five minutes, turning once, until the edges are deeply browned and the centers turn creamy.
Stir the yogurt with a spoonful of water and a little seasoning until it loosens enough to spread.
Spread the yogurt across a wide plate.
Pile the hot zucchini on top and serve right away, while the contrast of hot and cold is at its best.

title: Golden Spinach and Bell Pepper Egg Wedge

steps.text: Cook the sliced bell pepper in olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat until it softens and sweetens, then add the spinach and let it wilt; spread the vegetables evenly in the pan.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, season them, and whisk briefly.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables, scatter the cheese on top, and drop the heat to low.
Cook slowly until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center of the egg, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Slide it onto a plate, cut into wedges, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Avocado and Cucumber Soup, Served Cold

steps.text: Roughly chop the cucumber, the avocado, and half the lemon, picking the seeds and peel out of the lemon flesh.
Blend with the yogurt until completely smooth, adding cold water a little at a time until it pours like thin velvet.
Season boldly; it should taste bright and just barely sharp.
Chill fifteen minutes, or set the bowl over ice for five if you are in a hurry.
Serve in cold bowls with a small squeeze of lemon on each.

title: Fork-Tender Lemon Potatoes with Crusted Edges

steps.text: Cut the potatoes into thick wedges and pile them in a roasting tin.
Toss with a generous amount of olive oil, the crushed garlic, and half the lemon juice; season well.
Roast at 200°C for about thirty-five minutes, turning once, until the outsides crust over and the insides feel creamy when a fork slides in.
Season again while they are hot, so it sinks in.
Finish with the rest of the lemon juice and the zest; eat while the edges are still crisp.

title: Tuna and Black Beans with Snapping Celery

steps.text: Drain the black beans and the canned light tuna very well; wet beans turn a salad sodden.
Slice the celery thin and add it to a bowl with the beans and tuna.
Dress with lemon juice and olive oil and season generously.
Turn everything together gently so the tuna keeps some big, rough pieces.
Eat straight away, while the celery still snaps.

title: Sweet Lemon Yogurt with Apple for Dipping

steps.text: Stir the yogurt in a small bowl until it loosens and turns glossy.
Add the honey and the lemon zest and stir until the swirls disappear.
Cut the apple into wedges and toss them with a little lemon juice so they stay pale.
Serve the dip alongside the wedges, or spoon the yogurt over them on a plate.
It is best right away, while the apple is crisp and cold.

title: Pasta That Cooks in Its Own Tomato Sauce

steps.text: Put the pasta, chopped tomato, garlic, olive oil, and about 700 ml of water into one wide pan.
Bring to a boil, stirring so the pasta does not stick, then lower to a steady simmer.
Cook until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid is gone, twelve to fourteen minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir hard for thirty seconds; the sauce should turn glossy and cling to every noodle.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts into the sauce, then season and serve from the pan.

title: Seared Chicken over Avocado and Crisp Lettuce

steps.text: Press the chicken breast to an even thickness by leaning on it with the bottom of a heavy pan, then season well.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet and sear the chicken until the underside is deeply golden, about five minutes.
Flip and cook until a food thermometer reads 165 °F at the thickest point of the chicken, then rest it on a plate for five minutes.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Slice the avocado and arrange it on lettuce leaves with a squeeze of lemon.
Top with the chicken in slices and a last drizzle of olive oil.

title: Crispy Corn and Bean Tortilla Melts

steps.text: Mash half the black beans roughly with a fork; they should hold together but keep some whole ones.
Warm the mashed beans with the corn in a small pan, stirring until steaming and glossy.
Scatter half the cheese over one tortilla, spread the bean and corn mixture on top, then add the rest of the cheese and cap with the second tortilla.
Melt the butter in a skillet and toast the filled tortilla until the underside is deep gold and crisp, then flip and crisp the other side.
Cut into wedges and serve while the cheese is still stretchy.

title: Saucy Cumin Beef in Lettuce Leaves

steps.text: Get a skillet properly hot, add the ground beef, and break it up with a wooden spoon as it browns.
Add the diced onion and the cumin and cook until the onion softens and the spice smells toasted.
Add the chopped tomato and let it simmer down into a loose, chunky sauce, about five minutes.
Check that a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the thickest part of the beef, crumbling any big pieces as you go.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Season well, then spoon the hot beef into crisp lettuce leaves and eat with your hands.

title: Seared Chicken Strips with Charred Peppers and Warm Tortillas

steps.text: Slice the chicken breast into strips and season them well.
Sear the strips in a very hot, dry pan without moving them for two or three minutes, until browned underneath, then turn.
Add the sliced bell pepper and onion and let them catch a little char at the edges, tossing now and then.
Cook until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest chicken strip, then squeeze the lemon over the pan and scrape up the browned bits.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for a few seconds a side and serve everything folded inside them.

title: Rice and Beans Dressed in Cilantro and Lime

steps.text: Warm the black beans in a small pan with a splash of water and a thread of olive oil until they are steaming and glossy.
Season the cooked rice with lime juice and a little olive oil, fluffing with a fork.
Build the bowls: rice first, then the warm beans spooned alongside.
Tear the cilantro over the top.
Add more lime at the table; the bowl should taste bright and fresh to the last bite.

title: Tacos of Blistered Sweet Potato and Beans

steps.text: Dice the sweet potato small, spread it on a tray, and roast at 220°C until browned at the edges and tender in the middle, about twenty minutes.
Warm the black beans gently with the cumin and a splash of water, mashing a few against the side of the pan.
Char the tortillas directly over a flame or in a dry pan until they blister and puff in spots.
Fill each tortilla with sweet potato and beans.
Finish with a squeeze of lime over each taco.

title: Golden Potato Breakfast Tacos with Cumin

steps.text: Melt the butter in a skillet and fry the small-diced potato over medium heat, turning now and then, until browned outside and tender when a fork slides in, ten to twelve minutes.
Season the potato with the cumin.
Pour the egg over the potato and scramble gently until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the softest curd, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until they soften and smell toasty.
Fill the tacos and eat hot.

title: Charred Corn and Zucchini with Lime Butter

steps.text: Set a dry pan over high heat and add the corn; let it sit without moving until the kernels blister and take on dark spots.
Add the butter, garlic, and diced zucchini and turn the heat down to medium.
Cook until the zucchini is tender with gold-brown patches and the butter smells nutty, five or six minutes.
Squeeze the lime over the pan and scrape up the browned bits.
Taste and season; serve hot from the pan.

title: Quick Beef and Bean Rice Bowls

steps.text: Brown the ground beef with the cumin in a hot pan, breaking the meat into small crumbles.
Cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the thickest part of the beef, then add the chopped tomato and let it simmer five minutes into a loose sauce.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the black beans in the same pan or a small one beside it, until steaming.
Build the bowls on a bed of rice.
Spoon the beef and beans over the rice and serve at once.

title: Salsa-Topped Avocado Toast

steps.text: Chop the tomato with a little of the onion into a rough relish; add lime juice and leave it to sit.
Mash the avocado coarsely with seasoning, keeping some chunks.
Toast the bread until well browned and crisp at the edges.
Spread the avocado thickly and spoon the relish and its juices on top.
Eat straight away, before the toast softens.

title: Simmered Chicken Soup with Crisp Tortilla Strips

steps.text: Bring a pot of water to a bare simmer and lower in the chicken breast.
Poach about fifteen minutes, until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest part of the chicken, then lift it out and shred it with two forks.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and the cumin to the poaching water and let it simmer ten minutes into a light broth, then return the shredded chicken.
Cut the tortilla into thin strips and toast them in a dry pan until crisp and gold.
Serve the soup with the tortilla strips on top and a good squeeze of lime.
Chill leftovers up to four days; reheat portions until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Folded Tortilla Toasts with Beans and Melted Cheese

steps.text: Mash the black beans roughly, then fry them in the butter with a splash of water until they turn thick and spreadable.
Season the beans well.
Spread the beans over the tortillas and cover with the cheese.
Fold each tortilla in half and toast in a buttered pan until crisp and golden on both sides, pressing down with a spatula.
Cut into wedges and serve hot, while the cheese pulls.

title: Sizzling Salmon Cubes with Avocado and Lime

steps.text: Cut the salmon into large cubes and season them well.
Sear the cubes in a very hot, dry pan, turning once or twice, until a food thermometer registers 145 °F at the center of a salmon cube.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Squeeze the lime over the hot cubes in the pan and lift them out.
Dice the avocado and turn it with the cilantro and a pinch of seasoning.
Pile the salmon on the avocado and serve immediately.

title: Eggs Simmered in Spiced Tomato Sauce

steps.text: Simmer the chopped tomato with the red pepper flakes and a good amount of seasoning until it thickens into a quick sauce, about eight minutes.
Make two wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover the pan and cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center of an egg, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until soft and pliable.
Slide the eggs and sauce over the warm tortillas and scatter the cheese on top.

title: Green Lime Rice under Golden Chicken

steps.text: Season the chicken breast well and brown it in a hot, dry, lidded pan on both sides, then lift it out.
Cook the diced onion in the same pan until soft and golden, scraping up the browned bits.
Add the rice, water, and the lime zest; tuck the chicken back in, cover, and simmer gently until the rice is tender and the water is gone, about eighteen minutes.
Rest the pan off the heat, then confirm a food thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the chicken reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Finish with the lime juice and the torn cilantro, fluffing the rice around the chicken.

title: Stew of Sweet Potato, Beans, and Toasted Cumin

steps.text: Cook the diced onion in a splash of water over medium heat, adding another splash whenever the pan goes dry, until soft and glassy.
Add the cumin and let it toast in the pan until fragrant, half a minute.
Add the diced sweet potato and chopped tomato, then pour in water to barely cover.
Simmer until the sweet potato is tender when a fork slides in, about twenty minutes, then add the black beans and cook ten minutes more.
Season well at the end; the stew is even better after a few minutes off the heat.

title: Scrambled Eggs with Crisp Tortilla Pieces

steps.text: Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the sliced bell pepper until soft and slumped, five or six minutes.
Tear the tortilla into bite-size pieces and let them crisp slightly in the butter.
Add the egg and scramble gently over low heat until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the softest curd, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Season with the cumin and a good amount of seasoning.
Serve straight from the pan, hot.

title: Chicken in Lettuce Leaves with Lime Crema

steps.text: Dice the chicken breast small and cook it hot in a dry pan, tossing only now and then so it browns in patches.
Cook until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest piece of chicken, then season boldly.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with the lime juice into a quick, pourable crema.
Spoon the hot chicken into crisp lettuce leaves.
Drizzle with the lime yogurt and finish with torn cilantro.

title: Charred Corn Dip with Beans and Lime

steps.text: Char the corn in a dry pan over high heat until the kernels blister and smell sweetly toasted.
Mash half the black beans with a fork and leave the rest whole.
Turn everything together in the pan with the sour cream, the lime juice, and the cumin, and warm it gently until steaming.
Season generously; it should taste bright from the lime and a little smoky from the char.
Serve warm, straight from the pan, for three or four people to graze.

title: Peppers Chopped into Beef and Rice with Melted Cheese

steps.text: Brown the ground beef in a wide skillet over high heat, breaking it into crumbles as it goes.
Cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the thickest part of the beef, then tip the beef onto a plate, keeping the pan fat behind.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Cook the chopped bell pepper in the pan until it softens and catches a little color, then add the chopped tomato and the rice.
Pour in water to cover the rice by a finger's width and simmer, covered, until the rice is tender, about fifteen minutes.
Return the beef to the pan, scatter the cheese on top, cover, and let it melt off the heat for a couple of minutes.
Season to taste and serve straight from the skillet.

title: Lime-Dressed Avocado and Cucumber Salad

steps.text: Halve the avocado, remove the pit, and slice the flesh right in the skin, then scoop it out with a spoon.
Slice the cucumber into thin half-moons and cut the tomato into wedges.
Whisk the lime juice with the olive oil until it looks cloudy and slightly thick.
Arrange the avocado, cucumber, and tomato on plates and spoon the dressing over.
Toss gently at the table so the avocado holds its shape, and season just before serving.

title: Pasta with Glossy Tomato and Butter Sauce

steps.text: Put a big pot of water on to boil and cook the pasta until it still has a little bite.
Meanwhile, cook the chopped onion in olive oil over medium heat until it turns soft and sweet, about 6 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato and let it simmer down until it looks jammy and darkens, 10 minutes or so.
Drain the pasta, saving a mug of the cooking water.
Off the heat, swirl the butter into the tomato sauce until it turns glossy, then toss with the pasta and splashes of the saved water until it clings.
Taste and season; it should taste sweet and rich.

title: Deeply Browned Mushroom and Garlic Pasta

steps.text: Cook the pasta in a big pot of water until it has a little bite, then drain and save a splash of the water.
Slice the mushrooms and brown them hard in butter over high heat, in batches if the pan is crowded, until they turn deep brown and squeak against the spoon.
Add the garlic for the last 30 seconds, just until it smells fragrant.
Pour in the milk and let it bubble 2 or 3 minutes, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Toss the mushrooms and sauce with the pasta, loosening with a splash of the saved water.
Taste and season before serving.

title: Bubbling Cheese and Broccoli Pasta

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400 °F and butter a small baking dish.
Cook the pasta 2 minutes short of the package time, then drain.
Cut the broccoli into small florets and steam until just tender and vivid green.
Warm the milk and butter in the empty pot, then stir in most of the cheese until it melts smooth.
Toss the pasta and broccoli with the sauce, scrape everything into the dish, and scatter the last of the cheese over the top.
Bake about 15 minutes, until it bubbles at the edges and browns in spots.
Chill leftovers up to four days; reheat portions until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Weeknight Tuna Pasta with Lemon and Peas

steps.text: Cook the pasta until it has a little bite, reserving a mug of the cooking water.
Warm the peas in olive oil in a wide pan until they are bright and steaming.
Add the tuna, breaking it into large flakes with a spoon.
Squeeze in the lemon, add the drained pasta, and toss with splashes of the saved water until it turns silky.
Taste and season generously, then eat right away while it is glossy.

title: Slow-Simmered Beef and Carrot Pasta Sauce

steps.text: Cook the pasta and set it aside with a mug of its cooking water.
Brown the ground beef in a wide pot over medium-high heat, crumbling as it browns, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F, then scoop it out.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Soften the finely diced onion and carrot in the beef fat over medium-low heat, about 10 minutes, until sweet and jammy.
Add the chopped tomato and return the beef, then simmer low and slow about 25 minutes, until the sauce is thick and glosses the spoon.
Toss with the hot pasta and a splash of the reserved water.
Chill any extras up to four days; when you reheat, a food thermometer should read 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Golden Garlic and Chili Pasta

steps.text: Cook the pasta until it has a little bite, saving a mug of the cooking water.
Slice the garlic thin and warm it gently in the olive oil over low heat, swirling now and then, until it turns pale gold and fragrant.
Take the pan off the heat and add the red pepper flakes so they bloom without burning.
Toss in the drained pasta with splashes of the cooking water and stir hard until the oil and water turn creamy and cling.
Taste and season, then eat immediately — this one waits for no one.

title: Golden Coconut Potato and Pea Stew

steps.text: Cook the diced onion in a splash of water over medium heat until it softens and turns golden, adding more water as the pan dries.
Stir in the cumin and let it sizzle a few seconds, until the pan smells warm and toasty.
Add the diced potato and enough water to half-cover, then simmer about 12 minutes, until a knife slides in with little resistance.
Pour in the coconut milk and add the peas; cook 5 minutes more so everything turns creamy.
Taste and season, then ladle into deep bowls.

title: Cheesy Spinach Tortilla Stack

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375 °F.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan with a splash of water, then cool it slightly and squeeze out every drop of water you can.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and most of the cheese, then add the squeezed spinach and turn it through.
Layer the filling between the tortillas in a small baking dish, finishing with a tortilla on top.
Pour any remaining egg mixture over and scatter the last of the cheese on top.
Bake about 20 minutes, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the middle of the eggs and the top is puffed and golden.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Let it sit 5 minutes before cutting into wedges.

title: Roasted Chicken and Sweet Potato Sheet-Pan Dinner

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400 °F.
Cut the sweet potato into rough chunks and the chicken into large pieces.
Toss everything with olive oil, cumin, and thick slices of onion until well coated.
Spread it all out in one layer — crowding steams instead of browns.
Roast about 30 minutes, turning once, until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the thickest piece of chicken.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes so the juices settle, then bring the tray to the table.

title: Rice Bowls with Buttery Creamed Corn

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it covered and warm.
Simmer the corn with the milk and butter about 8 minutes, until the kernels plump and the milk thickens slightly.
Taste and season — the corn should taste sweet and rich.
Add the cheese and let everything rest off the heat 2 minutes so it melts in.
Spoon the creamed corn over the rice and eat it while it is hot.

title: Griddle-Crisped Tomato Cheese Sandwich

steps.text: Butter the outside of each slice of bread.
Layer the cheese and thin slices of tomato between the slices, buttered side out.
Cook on a griddle or skillet over medium heat until the bread turns deep gold and the cheese starts to ooze at the edges.
Rest the sandwich a minute before cutting so the filling holds together.

title: Garlic Tomato Toast with Fried Egg

steps.text: Fry the bread in olive oil over medium heat until golden and crisp on both sides, then set it aside.
In the same pan, cook the garlic about 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the chopped tomato and let it collapse into a rough sauce.
Crack in the eggs and cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F with the yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Stack the garlicky tomato on the fried bread and top with the eggs.
Eat right away, while the edges are still crisp.

title: Roasted Zucchini Pasta with Bubbling Cheese Top

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425 °F, toss the diced zucchini with olive oil, and roast until browned at the edges, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta until just shy of tender and drain.
Simmer the chopped tomato in a little olive oil until it turns thick and saucy, about 10 minutes.
Toss the sauce with the pasta and the roasted zucchini, scrape into a baking dish, and top with the cheese.
Bake about 15 minutes, until the top is spotted brown and bubbling at the edges.
Cover and refrigerate extras up to four days, then reheat until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the center.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Creamy Stovetop Rice with Honey Butter

steps.text: Put the rice and milk in a small pot and bring it up to a bare simmer.
Cook over low heat, stirring often so the bottom never catches, until the rice is soft and the mixture turns thick and creamy, about 15 minutes.
Swirl in the honey and butter until glossy and fragrant.
Serve warm in small bowls, while it still wobbles like custard.

title: Caramelized Onion Beef over Rice

steps.text: Start the rice first so it is ready when the beef is.
Melt the butter and brown the ground beef over medium-high heat, crumbling as it browns, until a food thermometer registers 160 °F; scoop it out.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Cook the sliced onion in the same pan over medium-low heat until it turns deep golden and sweet, 10 minutes or more.
Return the beef, pour in the milk, and simmer until it makes a light gravy.
Taste and season well, then spoon over the rice.

title: Velvet Carrot Soup with Fresh Ginger

steps.text: Melt the butter and soften the diced onion over medium heat until it turns sweet and glassy.
Add the sliced carrot and grated ginger and cook 5 minutes, until the ginger smells bright.
Pour in water to just cover and simmer until the carrot is tender all the way through, about 15 minutes.
Blend until completely smooth, then return to the pot and loosen with the milk.
Taste and season — it should taste sweet, warm, and a little zingy.
Cool leftovers, chill up to four days, and reheat until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Velvety Potato Soup with Celery and Onion

steps.text: Melt the butter and cook the diced onion over medium heat until it softens and smells sweet.
Add the sliced celery and diced potato, turn to coat, and cook 3 or 4 minutes.
Cover with water and simmer until everything collapses when pressed with a spoon, about 20 minutes.
Blend smooth, then loosen with the milk until it ribbons off the ladle.
Season generously — celery needs it to sing.
Chill what is left for up to four days; reheat until a food thermometer registers 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Egg Ribbon Soup with Tomato and Rice

steps.text: Simmer the chopped tomato in olive oil until it breaks down and turns saucy, about 8 minutes.
Add water and the rice and simmer until the rice is tender and the soup has body.
Whisk the eggs, then drizzle them slowly into the bubbling soup while moving the spoon in slow circles.
Give the soup a moment to settle, then check that a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the egg ribbons.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Taste and season, then shower with sliced green onion.
Cool the rest, chill up to four days, and reheat until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Soft Green Pea Soup with a Yogurt Swirl

steps.text: Melt the butter and soften the chopped onion until it turns sweet and glassy.
Tip in the peas with only enough water to cover them, then simmer 5 minutes until they are bright green and tender.
Blend until smooth and vivid.
Off the heat, swirl in the yogurt — boiling it would split.
Serve warm rather than hot, so it tastes fresh and sweet.
Chill leftovers up to four days; reheat gently until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Deeply Browned Mushroom Rice Soup

steps.text: Brown the mushrooms in olive oil over high heat until they turn deep brown and squeak against the spoon.
Add the diced onion and carrot and cook until they soften and pick up color.
Add the rice, give everything a turn to coat, then pour in about a litre of water.
Simmer until the rice is soft and the soup smells earthy, about 20 minutes.
Taste and season well, then rest the pot 10 minutes off the heat so the soup thickens.
Cool and chill the leftovers up to four days; reheat until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Restorative Ginger Soup with Shredded Chicken and Rice

steps.text: Bring about a litre of water to a gentle simmer with the sliced ginger and crushed garlic.
Lower in the whole chicken breast and poach gently until a food thermometer reads 165 °F at its thickest point, about 15 minutes.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Lift the chicken out, shred it with two forks, and return it to the pot.
Add the rice and simmer until it is soft and the cooking liquid tastes gingery all the way through.
Season, then top each bowl with sliced green onion.
Chill leftovers up to four days; when you reheat, a food thermometer should read 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Rustic Tomato Chickpea Stew with Soft Spinach

steps.text: Soften the diced onion in olive oil until it turns sweet and glassy.
Add the chopped tomato and cook it down about 10 minutes, until it darkens and the oil shimmers at the edges.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water and simmer 10 minutes more, until the stew thickens.
Wilt in the spinach at the very end, just until it turns glossy green.
Taste and season, finish with a thread of olive oil, and eat from deep bowls.

title: Skillet Eggs and Tomato, Diner Style

steps.text: Whisk the eggs, then cook them in olive oil over medium heat, moving the spoon slowly, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F; slide them onto a plate.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Cook the chopped tomato in the same pan until it turns saucy and the edges caramelize.
Season with soy sauce and take the pan off the heat.
Return the eggs in big ribbons and give one gentle turn.
Spoon into bowls and scatter with sliced green onion.

title: Silky Tofu Ribbon Soup with Green Peas

steps.text: Simmer the milk with an equal part of water and the soy sauce in a small pot.
Add the cubed tofu and the peas and heat until the peas are bright and floating.
Whisk the eggs, then drizzle them in slowly while moving the spoon in gentle circles; let the soup bubble softly about 2 minutes, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Taste and season just before ladling.
Spoon leftovers into a container, chill up to four days, and reheat until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Skillet Beef Rice with Sweet Peas

steps.text: Brown the ground beef with the diced onion over medium-high heat, crumbling as it browns, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Sprinkle in the cumin and let it sizzle until fragrant.
Add the raw rice, turn to coat, then pour in hot water to cover by about an inch.
Cover and simmer until the rice is nearly tender, about 12 minutes.
Add the peas, cover again, and cook 3 minutes more, until they are bright and plump.
Rest off the heat 5 minutes, then taste and season.

title: Crispy Potato Hash with Salmon Chunks

steps.text: Fry the diced potato in olive oil in a covered pan over medium heat until a knife slides in easily, about 10 minutes.
Uncover, raise the heat, and let the potatoes brown and crackle, turning only now and then.
Push the potatoes to one side and cook the onion until it softens and picks up color.
Nestle the salmon chunks among the potatoes and cook gently until a food thermometer reads 145 °F at the thickest point.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Squeeze over the lemon, give one careful toss, and eat while the edges are still crackly.

title: Garlicky Wilted Spinach with Crisp Tofu

steps.text: Pat the tofu dry and fry the cubes in olive oil over medium-high heat until golden and crisp on several sides, then lift them out.
Cook the garlic in the same pan for 30 seconds, just until it smells fragrant.
Add the spinach in handfuls, letting each handful wilt down before adding more.
Return the tofu, add the soy sauce, and give everything a toss until glossy.
Eat hot, straight from the pan.

title: Honeyed Apple Baked Oats

steps.text: Set the oven to 375 °F.
Slice the apples and lay them over the bottom of the dish.
Whisk the oats, milk, eggs, and honey into a loose batter.
Pour it over the apples and let it soak in for a few minutes.
Bake about 25 minutes, until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center of the eggs and the top is golden and barely springy.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Serve warm, cut into squares.

title: Thin-Crust Tortilla Pizza with Spinach

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425 °F.
Spread the tomato thinly over each tortilla, all the way to the edges.
Scatter over the cheese and the spinach leaves.
Bake right on the oven rack until the edges are crisp and the cheese bubbles, about 8 minutes.
Cut into wedges and eat hot, while the base crackles.

title: Mashed Chickpea and Tuna Toast with Lemon

steps.text: Crisp the bread until it is golden and sturdy.
Roughly mash the chickpeas with the lemon juice and olive oil, leaving some texture.
Break the tuna into large flakes and turn it gently through the mash.
Taste and season generously.
Pile onto the hot bread and eat while the edges are still crisp.

title: Crisp Chicken Salad with Lemony Yogurt Dressing

steps.text: Pan-fry the chicken over medium heat until a food thermometer registers 165 °F in the thickest piece, then rest it 5 minutes and slice.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice and a little grated cheese; taste for tang.
Tear the lettuce and toss it with most of the dressing until every leaf glistens.
Top with the warm chicken and the last drizzle of dressing.
Pack the dressing separately if this is going into a lunchbox.

title: Creamy Avocado Tuna in Lettuce Cups

steps.text: Mash the avocado with the lime juice and olive oil until smooth and pale.
Break the tuna into large flakes and gently turn it through the avocado.
Taste and season well.
Spoon into crisp lettuce leaves, letting them cup like little boats.
Eat with your hands, right away.

title: Salted Cucumber and Tomato Summer Salad

steps.text: Slice the cucumber paper-thin, season it lightly, and let it sit 10 minutes.
Drain off the water the cucumber has drawn out and pat it dry.
Toss with the tomato wedges, the lemon juice, and the olive oil.
Add the sliced onion for bite, as much as you like.
Chill 15 minutes before serving so everything turns cold and crisp.

title: Charred Zucchini and Chickpea Warm Salad

steps.text: Pull a vegetable peeler down the zucchini to make wide ribbons.
Char the ribbons in a dry, very hot pan until they blister and curl, working in batches.
Add the chickpeas, garlic, and a thread of olive oil and toss until the garlic smells fragrant and the chickpeas are hot.
Off the heat, dress with the lemon juice and the rest of the olive oil.
Taste and season generously; serve while it is still warm.

title: Soft Egg and Avocado Spinach Bowl

steps.text: Lower the eggs into simmering water and cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F with the yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Plunge them into ice water, then peel.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan with a splash of water, then season it well.
Slice the avocado and arrange it over the warm spinach.
Halve the eggs and set them on top.
Add a spoonful of yogurt and a squeeze of lemon to finish.

title: Seared Salmon over Crunchy Cucumber Lettuce

steps.text: Sear the salmon in olive oil over medium-high heat until a food thermometer reads 145 °F at its thickest point, then rest it on a plate.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Squeeze the juice from half the lemon into a bowl and whisk in the rest of the olive oil.
Shave the cucumber into ribbons and toss with the torn lettuce and the dressing.
Break the salmon into big flakes over the top.
Eat soon, while the salmon is still faintly warm.

title: Lemony Chicken Salad with Yogurt and Celery

steps.text: Poach the chicken gently in simmering water until a food thermometer reaches 165 °F, about 12 minutes, then cool it slightly and dice small.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Stir the yogurt with the lime juice until smooth.
Add the chicken, the finely sliced celery, and the chopped cilantro, and turn everything together.
Taste and season well; it should taste bright and creamy.
Chill 10 minutes if you can wait, then spoon into a container or eat straight away.

title: Cumin-Roasted Carrot and Chickpea Bowl with Yogurt

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400 °F and toss the carrots with the cumin and a splash of water so the spice coats every piece.
Roast until the edges caramelize and the carrots smell sweet, about 25 minutes.
Add the chickpeas to the tray for the last 10 minutes so they puff and turn golden.
Stir the yogurt with the lemon juice until loose and tangy.
Build the bowl: a swoosh of yogurt, warm carrots, toasted chickpeas.
Taste and season just before it goes to the table.

title: Sesame Cucumber and Carrot Slaw

steps.text: Cut the cucumber and carrot into thin matchsticks.
Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, and lime juice into a quick dressing.
Toss the vegetables with the dressing and let it all sit 5 minutes so they soften slightly.
Taste — it should hit salty, sour, and nutty notes all at once.
Serve cold, straight from the fridge if you have time to chill it.

title: Lemony Egg and Avocado Plates

steps.text: Lower the eggs into simmering water and cook until a food thermometer reads 160 °F, about 8 minutes; cool them under cold running water, then peel and halve.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Scoop the avocado from its skin and cut it into wide crescents.
Tear the lettuce into big pieces and divide it between two plates.
Arrange the avocado and the egg halves on the lettuce.
Squeeze lemon over everything, drizzle with olive oil, and season generously.

title: Broccoli with Warm Garlic-Lemon Oil

steps.text: Cut the broccoli into small florets and thin slices of stem so it cooks evenly.
Steam about five minutes, until a knife slides into the stem with just a little resistance.
Meanwhile, warm the sliced garlic in olive oil over low heat until it smells sweet and turns pale gold.
Drain the broccoli well and toss it through the garlic oil.
Finish with a good squeeze of lemon and season to taste.

title: Honey-Drizzled Apple and Cheese Bowl

steps.text: Dice the apple small, skin on, for color and crunch.
Spoon the yogurt into two wide bowls.
Crumble the cheese over the yogurt.
Pile the apple on top and drizzle honey over everything.
Taste and add another thread of honey if the apple runs tart.

title: Skillet Chicken with Lemony Greens

steps.text: Pat the chicken dry and season it well on both sides.
Sear it in olive oil over medium-high heat until deeply golden, 4-5 minutes a side.
Lower the heat and cook until a food thermometer registers 165 °F in the thickest piece.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Move the chicken to a plate to rest; steam the broccoli until bright green and just tender.
Add the spinach to the warm pan and toss it in the pan juices until it slumps and glosses.
Squeeze lemon over the greens, then plate them under the sliced chicken with a last drizzle of olive oil.

title: Peanutty Tofu Rice Bowls with Wilted Spinach

steps.text: Cube the tofu, pat it dry, and crisp it in a dry nonstick pan over medium-high heat until the edges turn golden.
Whisk the peanut butter with hot water and a splash of soy sauce until it loosens into a smooth, pourable sauce.
Add the spinach to the warm pan and toss just until it wilts.
Fluff the warm rice into bowls and top with the tofu and spinach.
Spoon the peanut sauce over everything right before serving.

title: Charred Corn Salad with Avocado and Lime

steps.text: Spread the corn in a dry skillet over high heat and let it char, tossing only now and then, until some kernels pick up dark spots.
Cool it a few minutes so the avocado stays creamy when it meets the pan.
Dice the avocado and fold it gently with the charred corn.
Dress with lime juice and olive oil, taste, and adjust the lime before seasoning.
Scatter the cilantro over the top just before serving.

title: Slow-Cooked Spinach and Mushroom Eggs

steps.text: Cook the sliced mushrooms in a dry pan over medium heat until they give up their liquid and it cooks off, then add olive oil and let the edges brown.
Add the spinach and toss until it wilts down.
Lower the heat, pour in the lightly whisked eggs, and cook gently, lifting the edges so the uncooked egg runs underneath.
Cover the pan, turn off the heat, and let it finish gently, about 3 minutes.
The eggs are ready when a food thermometer reads 160 °F in the center, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Cut into wedges and serve warm from the pan.

title: Golden Sweet Potato Bowls with Yogurt, Honey, and Oats

steps.text: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into chunks; steam or simmer until a fork slides in with no fight.
Mash the warm chunks roughly with a fork, leaving plenty of texture.
Spread the yogurt across the bottom of two bowls.
Spoon the sweet potato over the yogurt while it is still warm.
Toast the oats in a dry pan until they smell nutty, then scatter them on top.
Finish with a generous drizzle of honey.

title: Tomato and Onion Plate with Lemon Dressing

steps.text: Slice the tomatoes thick, about half an inch, and the onion as paper-thin as you can manage.
Shingle the tomato slices across a platter and scatter the onion over and between them.
Whisk the lemon juice with the olive oil and spoon it over the top.
Season generously and let the plate sit 10 minutes so the juices mingle with the dressing.
Serve at room temperature, spooning the pink-tinted juices back over the slices.

title: Cucumber Rice Lunch Bowl with Soy and Egg

steps.text: Cook the rice and spread it on a plate to cool quickly, or use yesterday's rice straight from the fridge.
Simmer the eggs until a food thermometer reads 160 °F, about 9 minutes, then cool them under the tap, peel, and halve.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Dice the cucumber into small pieces.
Toss the cooled rice with the soy sauce and the cucumber.
Pile into a bowl and lay the egg halves on top.
Scatter sliced green onion over everything.

title: Limey Chickpea Wraps with Peanut Butter and Lettuce

steps.text: Drain the chickpeas and mash them roughly with the lime juice, leaving some chunks for bite.
Spread the peanut butter in a thin layer across each tortilla.
Pile the mashed chickpeas down the middle and top with shredded lettuce.
Taste the filling and add another squeeze of lime if it needs brightness.
Roll the wraps up tightly, then halve on the diagonal.

title: Garlicky Simmered Rice with Golden Chicken

steps.text: Season the chicken and brown it in olive oil in a wide pan until the surface is deep gold; move it to a plate.
Soften the diced onion in the same pan, scraping up the browned bits, then add the minced garlic for the last minute.
Add the rice and toss to coat it in the oil, then pour in hot water.
