Nestle the chicken on top, cover, and simmer on low until the rice is tender and the liquid is gone, about 18 minutes.
Lift the chicken out and check it with a food thermometer until it registers 165 °F deep in the meat.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then serve it over the rice.

title: Sticky Honey and Soy Chicken with Garlic

steps.text: Season the chicken and sear it in olive oil over high heat, turning once, until both sides are deeply colored.
Add the sliced garlic for the last minute of searing, just until it turns fragrant.
Stir the honey and soy sauce together with a spoonful of water.
Pour the sauce into the pan and let it bubble until it thickens to a syrup that coats the back of a spoon.
Turn the chicken in the glaze and keep cooking until a food thermometer reads 165 °F at the thickest point.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Rest a few minutes, then spoon the sticky pan sauce over the top.

title: Butter-Basted Salmon over Soy Rice

steps.text: Season the salmon and sear it skin-side down in half the butter until the skin turns crisp and golden.
Flip the fillet, add the rest of the butter, and tilt the pan, spooning the foaming butter over the salmon for about 2 minutes.
Keep going until a food thermometer reaches 145 °F at the thickest point.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Season the warm rice with soy sauce and divide it between bowls.
Lift the salmon onto the rice in big pieces.
Pour the pan butter over everything and finish with sliced green onion.

title: Eggs Nestled in Cumin Tomato Sauce

steps.text: Soften the diced onion in olive oil until it turns sweet and floppy.
Add the cumin and toast it in the oil for a few seconds, just until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomato and cook until it breaks down into a thick, brick-red sauce, 10 minutes or so.
Make small wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and simmer on low until a food thermometer reads 160 °F in an egg, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Season and serve straight from the pan.

title: Gingered Ground Beef with Soy Pasta

steps.text: Cook the pasta, drain it, and toss with a tiny splash of soy sauce so it does not stick.
Grate the ginger and slice the onion thin.
Brown the ground beef in a hot pan until a food thermometer reads 160 °F, crumbling as it browns.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Add the onion and ginger and keep frying until the onion softens and the ginger smells bright.
Add the pasta and soy sauce and toss until everything turns glossy and well coated.
Serve in deep bowls while steaming.

title: Layered Tortilla and Black Bean Melt

steps.text: Simmer the black beans with the chopped tomato, cumin, and a splash of water until thick and fragrant, about 10 minutes.
Heat the oven to hot while you build the layers.
Layer tortillas and the bean mixture in a baking dish, scattering cheese between each layer.
Finish with a thick blanket of cheese on top.
Bake until the whole dish bubbles at the edges and the cheese browns in spots, about 20 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes so it holds together, then cut into squares.

title: Pan Salmon with Peas and Lemon Rice

steps.text: Cook the rice and drop the frozen peas in for the last 3 minutes, then drain.
Melt half the butter in a nonstick pan and sear the salmon until the underside turns golden.
Turn the fillets, add the lemon juice and the rest of the butter, and spoon the bubbling pan juices over the salmon.
Keep cooking until a food thermometer registers 145 °F in the thickest fillet.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Serve the salmon beside the buttery rice and peas, with every drop of the pan juices poured over.

title: Cumin-Scented Coconut Chickpea Bowl with Spinach

steps.text: Spoon the thick top layer from the can of coconut milk into a pan and soften the diced onion in it until sweet and floppy.
Add the cumin and toast it a few seconds, until the pan smells warm and spicy.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk and the drained chickpeas and simmer until mellow and slightly thickened, about 15 minutes.
Add the spinach and stir just until it wilts into the sauce.
Taste and season, then give it a minute off the heat before serving.

title: Cheesy Baked Potato and Egg Slices

steps.text: Slice the potatoes thin and parboil them 5 minutes, until a knife just pierces a slice.
Butter a baking dish and shingle the drained potato slices across it.
Whisk the eggs with the milk in a bowl and season generously.
Pour the egg mixture over the potatoes and scatter the cheese on top.
Bake in a hot oven until the top is puffed and golden, about 30 minutes.
Before serving, check the center of the dish with a food thermometer until it registers 160 °F, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Rest 5 minutes, then cut into wedges.

title: Ginger Broth with Tofu and Pasta

steps.text: Bring a liter of water to a simmer with the sliced ginger and soy sauce, and let it steep until the broth smells warm and gingery.
Add the cubed tofu and poach it gently for 5 minutes.
Drop in the pasta and cook until tender with a little bite.
Ladle into deep bowls and finish with plenty of sliced green onion.
Chill leftovers up to four days; reheat portions until a food thermometer registers 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Milk-Simmered Mushrooms over Rice

steps.text: Cook the rice and keep it covered.
Brown the mushrooms in butter over medium-high heat until the edges turn deep gold, then scoop them out.
Cook the sliced onion slowly in the same pan until it collapses into sweetness, 8-10 minutes.
Pour in the milk and let it bubble gently until it thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Return the mushrooms and let them steep a minute in the sauce.
Spoon the sauce and mushrooms over the rice and season generously.

title: Limey Chicken and Bean Skillet with Cumin

steps.text: Dice the chicken and toss it with the cumin until every piece is coated.
Brown it in a dry nonstick pan over medium-high heat, turning once, until golden on all sides.
Add the diced onion and cook until soft and fragrant.
Add the black beans with a splash of water and simmer, scraping the pan, until the sauce thickens slightly.
It is ready when a food thermometer registers 165 °F in the biggest piece.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Finish with a good squeeze of lime.

title: Egg and Tomato Rice Porridge

steps.text: Simmer the rice in a liter of water, stirring now and then, until the grains swell and the mixture turns creamy, about 25 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato and the olive oil and simmer 5 minutes more, until the tomato slumps into the porridge.
Drizzle the eggs in a thin stream, wait a few seconds, then drag a spoon through once so they break into soft ribbons.
Check the porridge with a food thermometer until it reads 160 °F, when the eggs are ready, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Season generously and finish with sliced green onion.
Extras keep four days in the fridge; reheat portions until a food thermometer reads 165 °F.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

title: Milk-Simmered Cheesy Rice with Broccoli

steps.text: Steam the broccoli until just tender and chop it small.
Warm the milk and butter in a wide pan until steaming.
Turn the heat low and melt in most of the cheese, stirring until smooth.
Add the rice and broccoli and stir until every grain is coated and creamy.
Slide the pan off the heat, scatter the last of the cheese on top, and cover until it melts, about 2 minutes.

title: Crunchy Apple Toasts with Peanut Butter and Honey

steps.text: Toast the bread until the edges turn deep gold and crisp.
Spread the peanut butter thickly while the toast is still warm.
Slice the apple thin and fan the slices over the peanut butter.
Drizzle honey over the top.
Cut each toast into triangles and serve right away so the edges stay crunchy.

title: Wok-Style Egg Rice with Carrots and Peas

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a wide pan until it shimmers.
Scramble the eggs fast, then slide them out when a food thermometer reads 160 °F, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Add a little more oil, then fry the finely diced carrot for about 3 minutes, until it turns tender and glossy.
Tip in the day-old rice and press it flat with a spatula so it crisps and turns golden at the edges.
Add the peas and return the eggs, breaking them into bite-size pieces as everything turns steaming hot.
Season generously and serve straight from the pan.

title: Garlicky Tomato Pasta with Wilted Spinach

steps.text: Cook the pasta and save a mug of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, sizzle the sliced garlic in olive oil until it smells sweet, then add the chopped tomato.
Simmer the sauce 10 minutes, until it darkens, thickens, and the oil gleams at the edges.
Add the pasta and toss, loosening with splashes of the cooking water until the sauce clings.
Take the pan off the heat and add the spinach, tossing just until it wilts into ribbons.

title: Sliced Chicken on a Garlic-Lemon Yogurt Bed

steps.text: Crush the garlic and stir it into the yogurt with a squeeze of lemon; let it sit while you cook.
Season the chicken and cook it in olive oil over medium heat until deeply golden on both sides.
Lower the heat, cover, and finish gently until a food thermometer reaches 165 °F in the center of the thickest piece.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice it against the grain.
Spread the garlic yogurt across a platter and lay the warm slices on top.
Finish with a drizzle of olive oil and another little squeeze of lemon.

title: Black Bean, Corn, and Pepper Lime Salad

steps.text: Rinse and drain the black beans until the water runs clear.
Dice the bell pepper small and toss it with the beans and the corn.
Dress with the lime juice and olive oil and season boldly.
Let the salad sit 10 minutes so the flavors meld and the pepper loses its raw edge.
Taste once more before serving — beans drink up lime.

title: Buttery Mushrooms and Onions on Toast

steps.text: Cook the sliced mushrooms in a hot dry pan, shaking often, until they squeak and give up their liquid.
Add the butter and the sliced onion and cook slowly until the onion turns soft, sweet, and golden.
Season generously.
Toast the bread and butter it while hot.
Pile the mushrooms and onions onto the toast and eat while the toast still crunches.

title: Roasted Sweet Potato Bowls with Cumin Chickpeas and Lime

steps.text: Cut the sweet potato into cubes and toss with olive oil and cumin until well coated.
Roast in a hot oven, turning once, until the edges are browned and the centers give easily to a fork, about 25 minutes.
Warm the drained chickpeas with a splash of water until they steam, then season.
Build the bowls with the sweet potato and chickpeas side by side.
Squeeze lime over everything just before eating.

title: Baked Tomato Cups with Egg and Cheese

steps.text: Halve the tomatoes and scoop out the seeds and pulp, leaving little cups.
Set them in a buttered dish and season the cavities.
Whisk the eggs with the grated cheese.
Fill each tomato cup with the egg mixture.
Bake in a hot oven until the filling is puffed, about 18 minutes.
Slide a food thermometer into the middle of a cup and check that it reaches 160 °F, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Serve warm.

title: Sesame-Soy Chicken with Cucumber Rice

steps.text: Dice the chicken and stir-fry it in a little sesame oil over high heat until golden on all sides.
Add the soy sauce and let it bubble into a quick glaze, about 30 seconds.
Keep the pan going until a food thermometer reads 165 °F in the largest chunk.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Slice the cucumber paper-thin and toss it with a few more drops of sesame oil.
Serve the glazed chicken over warm rice with the cucumber alongside.

title: One-Pot Rice with Chickpeas and Carrot

steps.text: Soften the diced onion and carrot in olive oil until the onion turns sweet and glassy, about 8 minutes.
Add the rice and toss to coat every grain in the oil.
Pour in hot water, add the drained chickpeas, and season.
Cover and cook gently until the rice is tender and has drunk up the liquid, about 18 minutes.
Rest off the heat 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

title: Open-Faced Tuna Melts with Corn and Cheese

steps.text: Drain the tuna and the corn well.
Break the tuna into chunks in a bowl and add the corn.
Pile the tuna and corn onto buttered bread and cover with a thick layer of cheese.
Grill until the cheese melts, bubbles, and browns in spots, 3-4 minutes.
Serve hot, while the cheese pulls in strings.

title: Lemony Chicken Wraps with Cucumber Yogurt Sauce

steps.text: Grate the cucumber, squeeze out the water, and stir it into the yogurt with a squeeze of lemon.
Cook the sliced chicken in a hot nonstick pan until golden on both sides.
A food thermometer stuck in the thickest piece registers 165 °F when the chicken is ready.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan until soft and pliable.
Spread the cucumber yogurt down each tortilla and add the chicken.
Roll tightly and halve.

title: Creamy Coconut Rice with Blistered Corn

steps.text: Simmer the rice in the coconut milk with a little water until the grains are tender and the kitchen smells sweet.
Fluff the rice with a fork and season.
Meanwhile, char the corn in a dry pan with a slick of olive oil until the kernels blister and pop.
Fold the charred corn through the rice.
Serve warm, with an extra spoonful of coconut milk on top if you like.

title: Eggs Baked in Chili Beans and Tomato

steps.text: Warm the olive oil with the red pepper flakes until they sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the chopped tomato and the black beans and simmer until the sauce thickens and darkens, about 8 minutes.
Press a well into the sauce for each egg and crack one egg into each well.
Cover and cook on low; the eggs are ready when a food thermometer registers 160 °F, yolk and white firm.

safety.source: USDA FSIS Safe Minimum Internal Temperature Chart, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/safe-temperature-chart/, retrieved 2026-10-11

steps.text: Season and bring the pan to the table.

title: Pasta Tossed with Broccoli and Golden Garlic

steps.text: Cook the pasta and save a mug of the cooking water.
Steam the broccoli florets over the pasta pot for the last 3 minutes, until just tender.
Warm thin slices of garlic in olive oil over low heat until pale gold and fragrant, never brown.
Add the pasta, broccoli, soy sauce, and splashes of cooking water, and toss until everything glistens.
Taste, adjust the soy sauce, and serve hot.

title: Warm Apple and Honey Yogurt with Toasted Oats

steps.text: Dice the apple small and warm it gently in butter until the edges turn glossy and the pan smells sweet.
Add a spoonful of honey and let it bubble into a quick syrup around the apple.
Toast the oats in a dry pan until they turn nutty and golden at the edges.
Spoon the yogurt into bowls and top with the warm apple.
Scatter the toasted oats over and finish with another thin thread of honey.
